exampleAnswers.title: Simplifying an Expression Using the Law that Conjunction Absorbs Disjunction

question.text:
Which of the following are logically equivalent to $Y?$

  1. $Y \land ( eg X \lor Y)$
  2. $ (Y \lor eg X) \land eg X$
  3. $( eg X \lor Y) \land Y$
question.explanation:
The law that conjunction absorbs disjunction is stated as

\[ Y \land (Y \lor \neg X ) \equiv Y. \]

With that in mind, let's inspect each of the given statements.

  • Statement I is logically equivalent to $Y.$ We have \[ \begin{align*} Y \land (\neg X \lor Y) &\equiv Y \land (Y \lor \neg X) \\[3pt] &\equiv Y. \quad \color{green}\checkmark \end{align*} \]

  • Statement II is not logically equivalent to $Y.$ We have \[ \begin{align*} (Y \lor \neg X) \land \neg X &\equiv \neg X \land (\neg X \lor Y) \\[3pt] &\equiv \neg X \not\equiv Y. \quad \color{red}\times \end{align*} \]

  • Statement III is logically equivalent to $Y.$ We have \[ \begin{align*} (\neg X \lor Y) \land Y &\equiv Y \land (Y \lor \neg X) \\[3pt] &\equiv Y. \quad \color{green}\checkmark \end{align*} \]

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and III only."
